notes: §1985:XII.3.4 GR6 (with Amendment 2's 6b sentence "Each lowercase letter is equivalent to the corresponding uppercase letter"): pseudo-text-1 matches only an equal ordered sequence of text words, comma, semicolon and space runs count as one space, operands are tried in order at each leftmost word, and the word after a match is the next leftmost. ApplyReplacements runs that cycle over TextWordScanner's words (separator comma/semicolon dropped), first operand wins, inserted text never rescanned; MatchesForReplacing folds case except in a nonnumeric literal's content (the COBOL character set exception), and the 2002 LEADING/TRAILING operands are refused at 85 (COBOL0900, probe g6b). Witness: ADD 1;   TO    W-A matches ==ADD 1 TO W-A== (5). Probes (classes a, b, c, d, f): lowercase pseudo-text matches uppercase source, 01 does not match 1, "abc" does not match "ABC", ADD 1, TO; W-A and a three-line ADD match, the inserted ADD 1 TO W-A is not rescanned (10, 13), an 18-digit negative MOVE is untouched, E(1) and E (1) both match an ODO element ==E (1)== (g6a, g6c); the first of ==XA== and ==XA XB== wins (g6d). The apostrophe literal (an implementor extension at 85, absent from the 1985 text) matches its quote form.

next.reason: Amendment 2 (X3.23b-1993) added to 6b 'Each lowercase letter is equivalent to the corresponding uppercase letter as specified for the COBOL character set' (§1985:XII.3.4 GR6; that definition, §1985:III.2, excepts 'nonnumeric literals and some PICTURE symbols'), so case folding is no longer a 2023 addition: §2023:7.2.4.4 GR8 c) 3 has it 'Except when used in the non-hexadecimal formats of alphanumeric and national literals'. The comparison cycle a to f is kept, but 2023 accepts operands 1985 refuses. 1985: 'pseudo-text-1 is compared to an equivalent number of contiguous source program text words'; 2023: 'pseudo-text-1 or partial-word-1 is compared to an equivalent number of contiguous source text-words', with 'When the LEADING phrase is specified, partial-word-1 matches the source text-word only if' its characters start the word (and TRAILING, end it). 2023 also adds matching equivalences 1985's 'equal, character for character' lacks: 'each alphanumeric character is equivalent to its corresponding national character', 'The two representations of the quotation symbol match', and compiler directive lines and comments 'treated as a single space'.
